caption:
Write items.length && in your machine coding round and the interviewer will point at the lonely 0 on the empty cart.

Look at the card. && returns its left side when the left side is falsy. With no items, items.length is 0, so the whole expression is 0, not false.

React renders nothing for true, false, null and undefined. It does render numbers. So 0 shows up on the page.

Make the left side a real boolean: items.length > 0 &&. Or use a ternary when there's an else branch.

The React docs list this exact case as a pitfall: don't put numbers on the left side of &&.

Source: react.dev, Conditional Rendering.
